newsitem.title: CHINA: China offshore oil plans to list investment arm.
newsitem.headline: China offshore oil plans to list investment arm.

text.p: China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) is looking at new ways to raise funds to boost downstream products and to develop overseas, including listing a subsidiary, state media said on Sunday.

CNOOC is creating an investment company in Hong Kong to raise funds, and expects to list the firm on the stock market, the China Daily Business Weekly said quoting CNOOC president Wang Yan. He gave no more details.
CNOOC expects to pump 16 million tonnes of oil and 8.5-10 billion cubic metres of natural gas a year by 2000, the newspaper said.
China's oilfields in the South China Sea produced 6.78 million tonnes of crude in the first half of this year, a 31 percent rise over the same period of 1996, latest figures showed.
The offshore oilfields are expected to boost crude oil output to 12 million tonnes this year from 11.84 million tonness in 1996.
